Oh, sleep... yes, sleep becomes quite unnecessary. During those times, I only need maybe two or three hours. I'll wake up long before dawn, and I just feel completely ready to go. I tell myself that sleep is really only for people who don't have an archive to rescue.

Well, let me think... yes, it's been longer than six months. I'd say the voices and that absolute certainty that people are watching my archive... it's been going on for about eight months now. 

Eight months... so that would mean it started right around the time the leaves were turning. I've always loved the autumn foliage. There's this one enormous Japanese maple in the botanical gardens that turns the most brilliant, violent shade of crimson. I used to try and sketch it, but colored pencils never quite capture the depth of that red. You really need a good watercolor for that, maybe an alizarin crimson mixed with just a touch of burnt umber. Watercolors are so unforgiving, though. She used turpentine to clean her brushes, and our little dorm room always smelled like pine and harsh chemicals. It gave me dreadful headaches, but she refused to switch to a less toxic solvent. She ended up moving to New Mexico, I think, for the light. Everyone says the light in Taos is spectacular for painting. Well, yes, I think I mentioned that a little bit ago, didn't I? There was that stretch of several weeks. I wasn't feeling grand or full of that buzzing energy, and I wasn't in one of those heavy, gray slumps either. I was just... ordinary. Doing my laundry, making my tea. Rubbing alcohol has such a sharp smell, it always reminds me of the nurse's office in middle school.

The packing tape always gets stuck to your fingers and leaves that awful sticky residue that you have to scrub off with rubbing alcohol. Rubbing alcohol has such a sharp smell, it always reminds me of the nurse's office in middle school. \n\nBut yes, even when my mood was perfectly fine, not high and not low, the whispers and the phone monitoring were still happening.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any recent head injury, new medical illness, or started any new medications or substances around the time these symptoms began?\n\nPatient: No, no head injuries. She said her granddaughter picked the color. Kids love those bright, neon colors, don't they? \n\nWhen I was a girl, everything was much more muted. Pastels, mostly. I had a lovely Easter dress once that was the exact color of a robin's egg, with little white lace around the collar. My mother made it herself on her Singer sewing machine. So many buttons in there... mother-of-pearl, heavy brass ones from old military coats, little wooden toggles. I'd arrange them all by size on the living room rug. \n\nBut what were you asking? ========== OUTPUT [patient] ==========
Well, yes, there are times... there are these days where I just feel absolutely radiant. Like I'm glowing from the inside out, and I feel so completely chosen, you know? Like I have this incredible, grand purpose. I'll have these brilliant plans, just so much energy buzzing through me. I'll stay up all night organizing my files and writing down these incredible ideas. I used to write everything down in those little marbled composition notebooks. I won the spelling bee in fifth grade with the word "chrysanthemum." It's such a lovely flower, isn't it? The deep burgundy ones are my favorite, they look so rich against the autumn leaves. I used to love pressing autumn leaves in heavy books. The encyclopedias were the best for that. We had a whole set of Encyclopedia Britannica, bound in that dark blue leather with the gold lettering on the spine... 

Oh, but you asked about the mood... yes, when I'm feeling that radiant, chosen way, if someone tries to tell me to slow down, or if they question my plans, I get furious. Just absolutely enraged. It feels like they're trying to erase me, to stamp out this beautiful, important thing I'm doing. It gets so intense that, well, yes, there was a time they had to take me to the hospital because I just couldn't function in the normal way anymore. I was too wrapped up in my purpose, and I was so angry at everyone trying to stop me.

He had this beautiful, heavy brass inkwell on his desk. I used to polish it for him on Sundays when I was a little girl. The polish smelled a bit like lemons, but chemical, you know? I can't imagine paying that just for a garnish. \n\nBut yes, the anger. I tell myself that sleep is really only for people who don't have an archive to rescue. \n\nYou know, dawn is actually the best time for natural light photography, anyway. The 'golden hour,' they call it. Though really, there are two golden hours, one in the morning and one right before sunset. The morning light always feels a bit cooler to me, a bit more crisp. I used to try to capture the frost on the wrought-iron fences in my old neighborhood during that morning golden hour. Wrought iron is so fascinating, isn't it? The way they twist the metal. They don't make fences like that anymore. Now it's all chain link or that terrible vinyl fencing that cracks in the winter. My neighbor put up a vinyl fence and it looked dreadful after just one season. She had this little yappy dog, a Pomeranian, I think, that would just hurl itself at the vinyl panels all day long. Well, it certainly made a mess of things, if I'm being honest. I completely lost the trust of my colleagues, and I was missing my board meetings... and my bills, too. The bills just piled up on the kitchen counter for weeks. I usually keep them in this lovely little wicker basket I bought at a craft fair in Vermont years ago. Vermont is just so beautiful in the autumn. The leaves turn these incredible shades of red and gold. We used to take driving tours up Route 100, stopping at all the little country stores to buy maple syrup. Real maple syrup, mind you, not that artificial corn syrup nonsense they sell in the plastic bottles at the grocery store. It makes such a difference on pancakes. I used to make blueberry pancakes from scratch every Sunday morning. You have to use fresh blueberries, though, the frozen ones make the batter turn a dreadful shade of gray... 

Anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the problems. Things got so out of hand that my cousin and one of the museum administrators actually had to step in. I just couldn't manage my appointments or handle my money safely on my own anymore, let alone go to public events.
